title: Project Overview and Architecture
content: This is an Expo-based mobile application with a Node.js backend. The system consists of two main components: expo_backend (Node.js REST API) and expo_mobile (React Native mobile app). The application serves as a platform connecting students, companies, and visitors for a software exhibition or expo event. The backend uses MySQL for data storage and AWS S3 for file storage, while the mobile app uses Firebase for real-time chat functionality. The architecture follows a RESTful API design with JWT-based authentication.

title: User Roles and Types
content: The system supports four distinct user roles: Student, Company, Visitor, and Admin. Each role has different permissions and access to different features. Students can create and manage projects, upload CVs and photos. Companies can create profiles with booth information and offerings. Visitors can browse projects and companies but have limited interaction. Admins have full access to view all users, projects, and companies.

title: Authentication System
content: The application uses JWT (JSON Web Tokens) for authentication. The authentication flow includes user registration, email verification with 6-digit codes, and login. Tokens are stored in AsyncStorage on the mobile app and have a 1-hour expiration time. The backend validates tokens using middleware that checks the Authorization header with Bearer token format. Password hashing is implemented using bcryptjs with a salt factor of 10. Email verification codes expire after 5 minutes.

title: Student Profile Management
content: Students can create and manage comprehensive profiles including personal information (name, email, university ID), academic details (major, year of study), skills (stored as JSON array), bio, profile photo, and CV. The profile photo and CV are stored in AWS S3 with organized folder structure. Students can update their profile information and upload/delete files. File uploads are limited to 10MB and support images and PDFs only. Profile photos are stored in student-photos folder and CVs in student-cvs folder.

title: Company Profile Management
content: Companies can create detailed profiles with company name, category, description, phone, address, booth ID, profile image, and website URL. The system links company profiles to user accounts and allows companies to update their information. Companies can upload a profile image which is stored in AWS S3. Each company is assigned to a specific booth at the expo, identified by booth_id. Companies can also create offerings to showcase their products or services.

title: Project Management System
content: Students can create and manage projects which are displayed at the expo. Each project includes title, description, video URL, GitHub link, and multiple project photos. Projects support collaboration - students can add a partner by email when creating a project. If the partner email exists in the system, they are automatically added as a project member. Projects are stored with a many-to-many relationship through the ProjectMembers table. Project photos are stored as JSON arrays in the database and uploaded to AWS S3 in the project-images folder. Students can upload up to 10 images per project.

title: Company Offerings Feature
content: Companies can create offerings to showcase products, services, or opportunities they provide. Each offering includes a name, description, price, and multiple photos. Offerings are linked to company accounts with a one-to-one relationship - each company can have one offering. Photos for offerings are stored in AWS S3 and managed as JSON arrays in the database. Companies can create or update their offering information.

title: File Upload and Storage System
content: The application uses AWS S3 for file storage with multer and multer-s3 for handling uploads. Files are organized in folders based on type: student-photos, student-cvs, project-images, and general images and pdfs folders. File uploads are restricted to 10MB maximum size. Only images (any image MIME type) and PDFs are allowed. Files are stored with private ACL, and access is provided through presigned URLs that expire after 1 hour (3600 seconds). The file naming convention includes folder, user ID, timestamp, and original filename.

title: Database Configuration and Connection Pooling
content: The backend uses MySQL database with mysql2 library and connection pooling for optimal performance. The pool configuration includes a connection limit of 10, unlimited queued requests, automatic waiting for available connections, and keep-alive enabled. The database connection is tested on startup and logs success or failure. Environment variables are used for host, user, password, database name, and port (default 3306). The pool uses promise-based API for async/await syntax support.

title: API Versioning and Endpoint Structure
content: The backend API uses versioning with the prefix /api/v1 for all endpoints. The main endpoint groups are: /api/v1/users for authentication and user management, /api/v1/students for student profiles and files, /api/v1/projects for project management, and /api/v1/companies for company profiles and offerings. Each endpoint group has its own route file and controller. The API follows RESTful conventions with appropriate HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE).

title: User Routes and Authentication Endpoints
content: User-related endpoints include POST /api/v1/users/send-code for sending verification codes (rate limited to 5 requests per 15 minutes), POST /api/v1/users/verify-code for code verification, POST /api/v1/users/login for user login (rate limited to 10 attempts per 15 minutes), and POST /api/v1/users/register for new user registration. All endpoints include input validation middleware. Verification codes are 6-digit numbers sent via email and expire after 5 minutes.

title: Student API Endpoints
content: Student endpoints include GET /api/v1/students for listing all students (admin only), GET /api/v1/students/profile/:user_id for getting student profile by user ID, GET /api/v1/students/email/:email for getting student by email, PUT /api/v1/students/profile/:user_id for updating student profile, POST /api/v1/students/profile/:user_id/upload for uploading photo and CV (rate limited to 20 uploads per hour), and DELETE /api/v1/students/profile/:user_id/file for deleting files. All endpoints require authentication token, and modification endpoints require authorization.

title: Project API Endpoints
content: Project endpoints include GET /api/v1/projects for all projects (admin), GET /api/v1/projects/myproject/:user_id for getting student's project, POST /api/v1/projects/myproject/:user_id for creating a new project, PUT /api/v1/projects/myproject/:user_id for updating project, POST /api/v1/projects/myproject/:user_id/upload for uploading project images (up to 10 images, rate limited), GET /api/v1/projects/all for all projects, and GET /api/v1/projects/all/except/:user_id for all projects except the user's own project. All endpoints require authentication.

title: Company API Endpoints
content: Company endpoints include GET /api/v1/companies for listing all companies, GET /api/v1/companies/profile/:user_id for company profile by user ID, GET /api/v1/companies/email/:email for company by email, PUT /api/v1/companies/profile/:user_id for updating company profile, POST /api/v1/companies/profile/:user_id/upload for uploading profile image, DELETE /api/v1/companies/profile/:user_id/file for deleting profile image, GET /api/v1/companies/offering/:user_id for getting company's offering, GET /api/v1/companies/offering/company/:company_id for public offering view, POST /api/v1/companies/offering/:user_id for creating offering, and PUT /api/v1/companies/offering/:user_id for updating offering.

title: Rate Limiting Strategy
content: The application implements in-memory rate limiting to prevent abuse. There are three rate limiting tiers: strict rate limiter (5 requests per 15 minutes) for verification code sending, auth rate limiter (10 requests per 15 minutes) for login attempts, and upload rate limiter (20 requests per hour) for file uploads. The rate limiter uses IP address for tracking and automatically cleans up old entries every 10 minutes. Rate limiting returns 429 status code with appropriate error messages when limits are exceeded.

title: Input Validation Middleware
content: The application includes comprehensive input validation middleware for all user inputs. Registration validation checks for valid name (non-empty string), email format using regex, password minimum length of 6 characters, and valid role (student, company, admin, or visitor). Login validation checks email format and password presence. Student update validation ensures proper data types for name, email, major, year, skills array, and bio. Project validation checks title, description, video URL, and GitHub link formats. Email validation uses the regex pattern /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.

title: Authorization Middleware
content: The authorization system uses two middleware functions: authenticateToken and authorizeUser. The authenticateToken middleware extracts the Bearer token from the Authorization header, verifies it using JWT with the secret key, and attaches the decoded user information to the request object. The authorizeUser middleware checks if the authenticated user is accessing their own resources or is an admin. If neither condition is met, it returns a 403 Forbidden response. This ensures users can only modify their own data unless they have admin privileges.

title: Email Verification System
content: The email verification system uses Nodemailer to send 6-digit verification codes via Gmail SMTP. Codes are randomly generated using Math.random() to create numbers between 100000 and 999999. Codes are stored in memory with a 5-minute expiration time. The system includes automatic cleanup of expired codes every 10 minutes. When users verify their code, the system checks if it exists, hasn't expired, and matches the submitted code. After successful verification, the code is deleted from memory. The email service uses Gmail with credentials stored in environment variables EMAIL_USER and EMAIL_PASS.

title: Environment Variables and Configuration
content: The application requires multiple environment variables for proper operation: JWT_SECRET for token signing, MYSQL_HOST, MYSQL_USER, MYSQL_PASSWORD, MYSQL_DATABASE for database connection, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION, S3_BUCKET_NAME for file storage, EMAIL_USER and EMAIL_PASS for email service, PORT for server port (default 5000), and optional CORS_ORIGIN for CORS configuration (defaults to allow all origins). The application validates all required environment variables on startup and exits if any are missing.

title: Error Handling and Logging
content: The application implements global error handling middleware that catches all errors. It handles specific error types including Multer file size errors (LIMIT_FILE_SIZE) and file type errors. In development mode, detailed error messages are returned; in production, generic error messages are used for security. All errors are logged to the console with descriptive prefixes. The application includes health check endpoint at /health that returns server status and timestamp. Database connection errors are logged with emoji indicators for better visibility.

title: CORS Configuration
content: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) is configured to allow requests from specified origins. The CORS origin can be set via the CORS_ORIGIN environment variable; if not set, it defaults to allowing all origins (*). The configuration includes credentials: true to allow cookies and authorization headers, and optionsSuccessStatus: 200 for legacy browser support. This enables the mobile application to communicate with the backend API across different origins.

title: Request Body Parsing
content: The server uses Express built-in middleware for parsing request bodies. JSON parsing is configured with a 10MB size limit to accommodate larger data payloads. URL-encoded data parsing is enabled with extended: true to support rich objects and arrays, also with a 10MB limit. This allows the API to handle file uploads and complex data structures efficiently.

title: Data Model: User
content: The User model represents all users in the system with fields: user_id (UUID primary key), name (full name), email (unique identifier for login), password_hash (bcrypt hashed password), role (student, company, visitor, or admin), and created_at (timestamp). The model provides methods to find users by email and create new users. Password hashing is performed before storage using bcryptjs with salt factor 10. Email is used as the unique identifier for authentication.

title: Data Model: Student
content: The Student model extends user information with academic details: student_id (UUID), user_id (foreign key to Users table), university_id, major, year_of_study, skills (JSON array), bio (text description), photo_name (S3 key for profile photo), cv_name (S3 key for CV file). Students can be linked to projects through the ProjectMembers junction table. The model includes methods to get student by user_id or email, update student information, and manage file uploads. Skills are stored as JSON strings and parsed to arrays when retrieved.

title: Data Model: Company
content: The Company model stores business information: company_id (UUID), user_id (foreign key), company_name, category (industry/type), description, phone, address, booth_id (expo booth assignment), profile_image (S3 key), website_url. Companies are linked to user accounts and can have one offering. The model provides methods to get company by user_id or email, update company information, and manage profile image uploads. All text fields default to empty strings when null for consistent frontend handling.

title: Data Model: Project
content: The Project model represents student projects with fields: project_id (UUID), title, description, video_url, github_link, project_photos (JSON array of S3 keys), status (pending by default), booth (booth assignment), created_at. Projects support multiple team members through ProjectMembers table. The model handles creating projects with optional partner email, updating project details, uploading images, and retrieving projects with associated student information. Project photos are stored as JSON arrays and parsed when retrieved. The system prevents duplicate projects per student.

title: Data Model: Offering
content: The Offering model represents company offerings with fields: offering_id (UUID), company_id (foreign key), name, description, price, offering_photos (JSON array of S3 keys). Each company can have one offering. The model provides methods to get offering by company_id, create new offerings, and update existing offerings. Photos are stored as JSON arrays in the database with actual files in S3. The system uses COALESCE in SQL updates to only update provided fields.

title: AWS S3 Integration
content: The application integrates AWS S3 using the AWS SDK v3 for Node.js. S3Client is configured with access credentials (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) and region from environment variables. Files are uploaded with private ACL, meaning they are not publicly accessible. Access is provided through presigned URLs generated using getSignedUrl from s3-request-presigner, valid for 1 hour. File operations include PutObject for uploads (handled by multer-s3), GetObject for generating download URLs, and DeleteObject for removing old files. The bucket name is configured via S3_BUCKET_NAME environment variable.

title: Presigned URL Generation
content: The system generates temporary presigned URLs for secure file access. When retrieving student profiles, company profiles, or projects, the backend automatically generates presigned URLs for associated files (photos, CVs, project images). These URLs are valid for 3600 seconds (1 hour) and allow the mobile app to download files directly from S3 without exposing AWS credentials. URLs are generated using GetObjectCommand and getSignedUrl from AWS SDK. The mobile app receives these URLs in API responses and can use them to display or download files.

title: File Deletion Strategy
content: When users upload new files to replace existing ones, the system implements a delete-before-update strategy. Old files are deleted from S3 before saving new file references in the database. For student files (photo/CV), individual files can be deleted via dedicated endpoint. For project images, all old images are deleted when new images are uploaded. Deletion uses Promise.allSettled to handle multiple file deletions, logging failures but not stopping the process. This ensures S3 storage doesn't accumulate unused files.

title: Mobile App Navigation Structure
content: The mobile app uses React Navigation with native stack navigator. The navigation structure includes authentication screens (Login, SignUp, Verify) and role-based main screens (Student, Company, Visitor). Additional screens include MyProject, MyOffering, ProjectDetails, CompanyDetailsScreen, StudentDetailsScreen, ChatListScreen, and ConversationScreen. The initial route is Login. All screens have headers hidden (headerShown: false) for custom header implementations. Navigation is centralized in App.jsx using NavigationContainer.

title: Mobile Authentication Flow
content: The mobile app authentication flow includes user registration, email verification, and login. Registration collects username, email, password, and user type (visitor, student, company). After registration, users receive a 6-digit verification code via email. Upon successful login, the app stores JWT token, user ID, and role in AsyncStorage. Navigation automatically redirects users to their role-specific screen (Student, Company, or Visitor). Token validity is checked to be within 7 days. Auth data includes token, userId, role, and loginTime.

title: AsyncStorage for Local Data Persistence
content: The mobile app uses AsyncStorage for persisting authentication data locally on the device. Stored data includes token (JWT), userId, role (user type), and loginTime (timestamp). The auth utility provides helper functions: getAuthToken, getUserId, getUserRole for retrieving data; storeAuthData for saving all auth data at once using multiSet; clearAuthData for removing all auth data using multiRemove; isTokenValid for checking if login is still within 7-day validity period; and getAuthHeaders for generating authorization headers for API requests.

title: Firebase Integration for Chat
content: The mobile app uses Firebase for real-time chat functionality. Firebase is configured with Firestore for database and Auth for user authentication with React Native persistence using AsyncStorage. The Firebase configuration includes API key, auth domain, project ID, storage bucket, messaging sender ID, and app ID. The chat system is separate from the main backend authentication, allowing real-time messaging between users. Firebase initialization is done once in firebase.js and exported for use throughout the app.

title: Chat Service and Firestore Structure
content: The chat service uses Firestore with two main collections: users (storing user profiles with type, name, email, photoUrl) and chats (storing conversation data). Each chat document contains members array (two user IDs), lastMessage, lastMessageTime, and unreadCount fields for each member. Chat IDs are generated by sorting user IDs alphabetically and joining with underscore for consistency. Messages are stored in subcollection chats/{chatId}/messages with fields: senderId, senderName, text, createdAt, isRead. The service provides real-time subscriptions using onSnapshot for live updates.

title: Real-time Chat Features
content: The chat system provides comprehensive real-time messaging features including: creating or getting existing chats between users, sending messages with automatic lastMessage updates, real-time message subscriptions with onSnapshot, marking messages as read with unread count reset, subscribing to all user chats sorted by lastMessageTime, subscribing to total unread count across all chats, and getting user data for displaying chat participants. Messages include read status tracking and sender information. The system uses Firestore server timestamps for accurate time tracking.

title: Firebase Authentication Service
content: The mobile app includes Firebase authentication supporting email/password and Google sign-in. The auth service provides: signInWithEmail for email/password login, signUpWithEmail for creating accounts with Firestore user document creation, signInWithGoogle using Google OAuth credentials, completeGoogleSignUp for adding user type after Google sign-in, signOut for logging out and clearing AsyncStorage, and getCurrentUser for getting the current Firebase auth user. The service integrates with the chat system by creating user documents in Firestore upon registration.

title: API Client Configuration
content: The mobile app uses axios for HTTP requests to the backend API. The base URL is configured based on server IP addresses with different options for different developers and networks (SERVER_IP_AYMAN, SERVER_IP_HOME_AYMAN, SERVER_IP_BAHA). The server port is configurable (default 5000). API endpoints are accessed via BASE_URL with versioned path /api/v1. All API calls include proper headers with Content-Type: application/json and Authorization bearer tokens where required.

title: User Registration API Call
content: The mobile app's user registration API client sends POST requests to /api/v1/users/register with body containing name, email, password, and role. The function handles three types of errors: server response errors (returns error message from response), no response errors (server unreachable), and request setup errors. Successful registration returns success status and user data. The function checks response.data.success to determine if registration was successful.

title: User Login API Call and Navigation
content: The login API client posts to /api/v1/users/login with email and password. On success, it extracts token, userId, and role from response, stores them in AsyncStorage using storeAuthData, and navigates to the appropriate screen based on role (Visitor, Student, or Company). The function handles errors similarly to registration, providing detailed error messages. Login success includes automatic navigation, eliminating the need for manual redirect logic in components.

title: Project Partner Collaboration
content: The project system supports team collaboration by allowing students to add partners when creating projects. When creating a project, students can provide a partner_email. The system looks up the student by email and, if found, adds them as a project member in the ProjectMembers junction table. If the partner email doesn't exist, the project is still created but only for the creating student, and a message is returned indicating the partner wasn't found. This allows flexible team formation while preventing errors if a partner hasn't registered yet.

title: Database Transaction Handling
content: The application uses database transactions for operations that modify multiple tables. For example, when updating student profiles, the system begins a transaction, updates the Users table (name, email) and Students table (major, year, skills, bio) separately, then commits the transaction. If any error occurs, the transaction is rolled back to maintain data consistency. Similar transaction handling is used for project creation with partners and company profile updates. Connection pooling ensures connections are properly released after transactions.

title: JSON Data Storage and Parsing
content: The application stores complex data as JSON strings in MySQL. Student skills are stored as JSON arrays in the skills column. Project photos and offering photos are stored as JSON arrays containing S3 file keys. When retrieving data, the application parses JSON strings back to JavaScript arrays, handling both string and already-parsed formats. The parsing includes error handling to return empty arrays if JSON is invalid. When saving, arrays are stringified using JSON.stringify() before database insertion.

title: Signed URL Security and Expiration
content: All file access from S3 uses presigned URLs for security. These URLs are temporary (1-hour expiration) and grant time-limited access to private S3 objects without exposing AWS credentials. When the mobile app receives these URLs, they can be used directly to display images or download files. After expiration, new URLs must be generated by calling the API again. This approach balances security (files are private) with convenience (clients can directly access S3). The backend generates fresh URLs on each API call.

title: Role-Based Access Control
content: The application implements role-based access control through authorization middleware and endpoint protection. Users can only access and modify their own resources unless they have admin role. The authorizeUser middleware compares req.user.userId with req.params.user_id to ensure ownership. Admin users bypass this check and can access all resources. Certain endpoints like getting all students or all projects are admin-only. Read endpoints for viewing other users' profiles (by email) are public but require authentication, enabling discovery while protecting modification rights.

title: Booth Assignment System
content: Both companies and projects can be assigned to booths at the expo. Companies have a booth_id field indicating their physical location. Projects also have booth assignment capabilities. This allows the expo to organize the physical layout with companies and projects at designated booths. The booth information is included in profile data so attendees can locate companies and projects at the event venue.

title: Image Upload Limits and Validation
content: File uploads are restricted by type and size. Supported file types are images (any MIME type starting with image/) and PDFs (application/pdf). Maximum file size is 10MB per file. Students can upload 1 photo and 1 CV. Projects can upload up to 10 images. Companies can upload 1 profile image. Offerings can have multiple photos. The multer fileFilter rejects invalid file types before upload. Size limit errors return specific 400 error responses. Upload endpoints are rate-limited to 20 requests per hour.

title: Search and Discovery Features
content: The application supports discovering other users and projects. Students can view other students' profiles by email, companies can be browsed in a list or viewed individually, projects can be viewed in a list excluding the viewer's own project. All list endpoints return comprehensive data including related entities (e.g., projects include associated students, students include project information). This enables attendees to explore participants and projects at the expo. Public viewing endpoints require authentication but allow cross-role access.

title: API Response Format Standardization
content: All API responses follow a consistent format with success boolean, message string, and optional data object. Successful responses include success: true, a descriptive message, and data containing the requested/modified resource. Error responses include success: false and an error message. This standardization makes client-side handling predictable and simplifies error handling. Status codes follow REST conventions: 200 for success, 201 for resource creation, 400 for validation errors, 401 for authentication errors, 403 for authorization errors, 404 for not found, 429 for rate limiting, 500 for server errors.

title: Development Dependencies and Tools
content: The backend development uses nodemon for automatic server restart during development. The dev script runs nodemon index.js for development with hot reload, while start runs node index.js for production. The project uses ES modules (type: module in package.json) allowing import/export syntax. Key dependencies include Express 5.1.0 for web framework, bcryptjs for password hashing, jsonwebtoken for JWT handling, multer 2.0.2 and multer-s3 for file uploads, mysql2 for database, AWS SDK v3 for S3, nodemailer for email, cors for cross-origin requests, dotenv for environment variables, and uuid for generating unique IDs.

title: Mobile App Dependencies and Frameworks
content: The mobile app uses Expo SDK ~54.0.7 with React 19.1.0 and React Native 0.81.4. Navigation is handled by React Navigation v7 with native stack navigator. Key dependencies include AsyncStorage for local storage, expo-image-picker and expo-document-picker for file selection, expo-sharing for file sharing, Firebase 11.10.0 for real-time chat and auth, axios 1.12.2 for HTTP requests, jwt-decode for token parsing, react-native-toast-message for notifications, expo-linear-gradient for UI gradients, react-native-reanimated for animations, and react-native-svg for vector graphics. The app targets multiple platforms (Android, iOS, web) through Expo.

title: UI Component Library and Styling
content: The mobile app uses custom components and styling. Main reusable components include MainButton for primary actions, Select for dropdowns, ChatListItem for chat preview items, and MessageBubble for individual messages. Styling uses React Native StyleSheet with expo-linear-gradient for gradient backgrounds. The color scheme is defined in constants/constants.js with a main blue color theme. Ionicons from expo vector icons provides icons throughout the app. The UI follows a modern, gradient-based design with card layouts and smooth transitions.

title: Form Validation in Mobile App
content: The mobile app implements client-side validation before API calls. Login validation checks for valid email format and password presence. Sign-up validation checks username, email format, password minimum length, password confirmation match, and user type selection. Validation errors are displayed inline using error state and error text components. The validation functions are in validationLogin.jsx and validationSignUp.jsx. Validation provides immediate feedback to users before making network requests.

title: Toast Notifications
content: The app uses react-native-toast-message for displaying notifications to users. Toast notifications provide non-intrusive feedback for actions like successful updates, errors, or confirmations. The Toast component is rendered at the root level in App.jsx, making it available throughout the app. Toasts can show success, error, or info messages with customizable duration and positioning.

title: Server Startup and Health Monitoring
content: The server starts on port 5000 (configurable via PORT environment variable) and listens on all network interfaces (0.0.0.0) for accessibility from other devices. On startup, it validates all required environment variables, tests database connection, and logs the server URL and API documentation endpoint. A health check endpoint at /health returns server status, success flag, and current timestamp. The root endpoint at / returns API version and available endpoint groups. Startup messages use emoji indicators for visual feedback in console.

title: Email Verification Code System Details
content: The verification code system generates random 6-digit codes (100000-999999) for email verification. Codes are sent via Nodemailer using Gmail SMTP. Each code is stored in memory with the email as key and an expiration timestamp (5 minutes from creation). The system includes automatic cleanup that runs every 10 minutes to remove expired codes and prevent memory leaks. Users must verify their code before it expires. The verification endpoint checks existence, expiration, and correctness of the code before confirming. On successful verification, the code is immediately deleted.

title: Project Status and Lifecycle
content: Projects have a status field that defaults to 'pending'. This allows for potential approval workflows where projects might need admin approval before being displayed publicly. The current implementation shows all projects regardless of status, but the infrastructure exists for implementing status-based filtering (e.g., pending, approved, rejected). Projects also track creation time with created_at timestamp. The project lifecycle includes creation by students, optional partner addition, image uploads, and updates to project details.

title: Multiple File Upload Handling
content: The application handles multiple file uploads using multer's fields() method. For students, both photo and cv can be uploaded simultaneously with maxCount: 1 each. For projects, up to 10 images can be uploaded at once using maxCount: 10. For companies and offerings, single file uploads are supported. The req.files object contains arrays of uploaded files organized by field name. File keys from S3 are extracted using file.key property. Multiple file deletions are handled using Promise.allSettled to continue even if some deletions fail.

title: Database Query Optimization
content: The application uses JOIN queries to retrieve related data efficiently. For example, when fetching student profiles, the query JOINs Users, Students, ProjectMembers, and Projects tables to get all related information in a single query. Similarly, company queries JOIN Companies and Users tables. When retrieving all projects, the system fetches associated students for each project. The use of connection pooling, async/await syntax with promise-based mysql2 API, and prepared statements (parameterized queries with ?) provides good performance and SQL injection protection.

title: Error Messages and User Feedback
content: The application provides clear, actionable error messages for common scenarios. For authentication errors, messages indicate whether email/password is invalid, token is expired/invalid, or user lacks authorization. For validation errors, specific field errors are returned (e.g., 'Valid email is required', 'Password must be at least 6 characters'). For file operations, messages indicate file type restrictions, size limits, or missing files. For rate limiting, messages explain the limit and suggest trying again later. Development mode shows detailed error messages while production mode shows generic messages for security.
